	What relevant goals will this unit address? 


1. Develop models to identify the parts of a plant—root, stem, leaf, and flower.

	Students will be able to independently use their knowledge to…

* plants are living things that have different parts to survive and grow (roots, stems, leaves)

* different animals use their body parts in different ways to help them survive and grow
* animals use their body parts in different ways to: see, hear, grasp objects, protect themselves, move from place to place, seek and find food, take in water, food and air

* What parts of plants/animals help them survive and grow?  
* How do plants/animals respond to their environment?
* How do the parts of plants and animals help them meet their needs?

* A short oral presentation with picture cards.

* What basic things animals need to survive in the garden. Make sure to name some animals that might visit!

STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
	TRANSFER
	What relevant goals will this unit address? 


1. Develop models to identify the parts of a plant—root, stem, leaf, and flower.
2. Ask questions to compare and contrast the basic needs of plants (air, water, light, and nutrients) and animals (air, water, food, and shelter).
3. Design a solution to ensure that a plant or animal has all of its needs met.


	Students will be able to independently use their knowledge to…
* compare and contrast the basic needs of plants (air, water, light, and nutrients) and animals (air, water, food, and shelter).
*  make a plan to help a plant and or animal meet its needs (providing water, shelter, light, food, etc.)


	MEANING
	UNDERSTANDING:
Students will understand that…
* plants are living things that have different parts to survive and grow (roots, stems, leaves)
* flowers and fruits are parts of many plants that help plants survive and grow
* plants respond to light
* different animals use their body parts in different ways to help them survive and grow
* animals use their body parts in different ways to: see, hear, grasp objects, protect themselves, move from place to place, seek and find food, take in water, food and air


	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS:
What questions will guide students' inquiry?
* What parts of plants/animals help them survive and grow?  
* How do plants/animals respond to their environment?
* How do the parts of plants and animals help them meet their needs?
* How are food and nutrients different for plants and animals? 


	ACQUISITION
	Students will know…
* the basic needs of plants and animals to survive in their environments.
* plants and animals are living things with basic needs like air and water, nutrients and shelter
* Animals and plants are similar and different


	Students will be skilled at…
* differentiate between how plants make their own food and how animals need to eat other things to survive 
*  identifying key parts of a plant (like leaves, stem, roots)
* recognize different types of animals in their environment
* compare and contrast the basic needs of plants (air, water, light, and nutrients) and animals (air, water, food, and shelter). 
* make a plan to help a plant and or animal meet its needs (providing water, shelter, light, food, etc.)

1 SCI UNIT 3: 1st Grade (Magnets)
STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
	TRANSFER
	Magnets
1. Students will explore how magnets are used in everyday life. 
2.  Students will investigate how magnets attract and repel one another. 
3. Students will explore how various objects will be affected by a magnet. 
4. Students will observe that motion is dependent on the strength of the push or pull to move objects attracted by magnets. 






	Students will be able to independently use their learning to…
Magnets
* Discover what magnets are and how they work. They will learn that magnets come in many shapes and sizes, and that they have two poles. These poles either attract or repel the poles of other magnets.
	MEANING
	UNDERSTANDING:
Students will understand that…


* Magnets attract and repel each other and certain kinds of other materials
* Magnets have different effects on some common objects
* When magnets attract an object, it pulls the object towards that magnet, causing it to move or stick to the magnet.
* When magnets repel each other, they push away.
* The ability of magnets to attract and repel each other in certain materials can be used to accomplish everyday tasks.


	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS:
Students will keep considering….


* How do we move things?
* Do objects move only when we touch them?
* Are there ways to move an object without touching it?
* What objects do magnets attract? 
* Why do magnets attract and repel each other? 
* How are magnets used in everyday life? 
* What are the similarities and differences between objects that magnets do and do not attract?
	ACQUISITION
	Students will know…


* Magnets have north and south poles, and opposite poles attract each other, while like poles repel each other
* Magnets have many uses, including in electric motors, hospital equipment, and storing metal tools
* The Earth is a huge magnet






	Students will be skilled at…


* Identifying objects that are attracted to magnets
* Asking questions, solving problems, and drawing conclusions about magnets
* Testing the magnetism of common objects
* Predicting the magnetism of common objects
* Explaining how magnets are used in everyday life

Learning Target: Students will know that magnets have north and south poles, and opposite poles attract each other, while like poles repel each other.

* DOK Level: Level 1 (Recall and Reproduction) - Recalling the basic properties of magnets.
	Success Criteria:
* I can identify the north and south poles of a magnet.
* I can predict whether two magnets will attract or repel each other based on their poles. (Connects to: understanding that opposite poles attract and like poles repel)


	

Learning Target: Students will know that magnets have many uses, including in electric motors, hospital equipment, and storing metal tools.

* DOK Level: Level 1 (Recall and Reproduction) - Recalling examples of magnet uses.
	Success Criteria:
* I can list three different ways magnets are used in everyday life. (Connects to: explaining how magnets are used in everyday life)
	

Learning Target: Students will know that the Earth is a huge magnet.

* DOK Level: Level 1 (Recall and Reproduction) - Recalling a specific fact about the Earth.
	Success Criteria:
* I can state that the Earth acts like a giant magnet.
	

Learning Target: Students will be able to identify objects that are attracted to magnets.

* DOK Level: Level 2 (Skill/Concept) - Students are applying their understanding of magnetism to identify magnetic materials.
	Success Criteria:
* I can test different objects and sort them into groups of "attracted to a magnet" and "not attracted to a magnet."
	

Learning Target: Students will be able to ask questions, solve problems, and draw conclusions about magnets.

* DOK Level: Level 3 (Strategic Thinking) and Level 4 (Extended Thinking) - This involves higher-order thinking skills.
	Success Criteria:
* I can ask a testable question about magnets.
*  can plan and conduct a simple investigation to answer my question about magnets.
* I can use my observations to draw a conclusion about magnets.
	

Learning Target: Students will be able to test the magnetism of common objects.

* DOK Level: Level 2 (Skill/Concept) - Students are actively investigating the magnetic properties of objects.
	Success Criteria:
* I can use a magnet to test whether different common objects are magnetic.
	

Learning Target: Students will be able to predict the magnetism of common objects.

* DOK Level: Level 2 (Skill/Concept) - Students are using their prior knowledge to make predictions.
	Success Criteria:
* Before testing, I can make a prediction about whether a common object will be attracted to a magnet and explain my reasoning.
	

Learning Target: Students will be able to explain how magnets are used in everyday life.
* DOK Level: Level 2 (Skill/Concept) - Students need to understand the application of magnets.
	Success Criteria:
* I can explain how a magnet is used in one specific everyday object (e.g., a refrigerator magnet, a can opener).
